final_answer:
**Short answer:** Yes. CAPA-26-008 and CAPA-26-016 trace back to the same upstream event: the FRZ-80-02 freezer failure in April 2026, which warmed the lentiviral vector lot LV25-118. Their recorded root causes differ (compressor failure vs. donor variability), but the data point to one cause. The link between the freezer and the vector is inferred from the data, and the CAPA-26-016 root cause is contradicted by it.

**CAPAs raised from deviations (trace_link RESULTED_IN equivalents)**
- CAPA-26-008 (corrective, closed, "effective") ← DEV-26-021: FRZ-80-02 high-temperature alarm, root cause "compressor failure (age-related)". Action: replace the compressor.
- CAPA-26-016 (preventive, open) ← DEV-26-027: low %CAR+ in ENG26-01/02, root cause "suspected donor variability (low CD3%)". Action: evaluate a minimum CD3% criterion.
- CAPA-26-012 (open, past due) ← DEV-26-011: INC-03 door alarm late, root cause "door switch misaligned".
- CAPA-26-015 (closed, effectiveness "PENDING") ← DEV-26-033: PPQ26-02 low viability, root cause "operator did not confirm door latch".
- CAPA-26-019 (open) ← DEV-26-041: tubing supplier weld defect. No link to the others.

**The shared cause: FRZ-80-02 thermal excursion affecting vector lot LV25-118**
- The historian shows FRZ8002 rising from about -80 °C to about -10 °C between 20 and 23 April, and not back below -78 °C until 23 April 16:00. DEV-26-021 records a maximum of about -36 °C before relocation.
- Lot LV25-118 is stored in FRZ-80-02 (material_lot). It was used for every transduction from PD26-014 onward.
- Transductions with LV25-118 before the excursion gave FC-CAR (%CAR+) of 34.5–41.3 (PD26-014 to PD26-023).
- Transductions with LV25-118 after the excursion gave 11.9–19.8: PD26-024 (17.3), PD26-025 (14.9), PD26-026 (16.3), PD26-027 (16.0), ENG26-01 (19.8), ENG26-02 (11.9), ENG26-03 (13.9).
- Donor CD3% does not explain the drop. ENG26-01 and ENG26-02 had CD3 of 65.3% and 63.8%, similar to or better than pre-excursion batches. PD26-023 had 65.0% CD3 and %CAR+ of 35.1%. ENG26-03 shows the same drop but is not listed in DEV-26-027.
- The vector CoA functional titer (FT_TU_ML, 104 × 10⁶ TU/mL) did not change, and the MOI was nominally 5.0 in every batch. So the potency loss is not visible in the uo04 record or the titer. The mechanism is a pattern-based inference, not a confirmed finding.

**Gaps to resolve**
- CAPA-26-008 was closed as effective based only on the compressor replacement and pull-down check. Nothing in the record assesses the vector lot that was in the freezer.
- DEV-26-021 says the vector was relocated to FRZ-80-01 at 15:30 on 20 April. The historian shows FRZ-80-02 still warm through 22 April, and material_lot still lists LV25-118 in FRZ-80-02.
- No trace link connects DEV-26-021 or DEV-26-027 to LV25-118 or to the affected batches.

**Weaker, separate link:** CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015 both concern the INC-03 door (DEV-26-011 and DEV-26-033). They share equipment and failure mode, but their recorded causes are different and there is no data here to show one caused the other, so I have not counted them as the shared cause.

```json
{"answer_ids": ["CAPA-26-008", "CAPA-26-016", "DEV-26-021", "DEV-26-027", "FRZ-80-02", "LV25-118"]}
```

content.text:
**Short answer:** Yes. CAPA-26-008 and CAPA-26-016 trace back to the same upstream event: the FRZ-80-02 freezer failure in April 2026, which warmed the lentiviral vector lot LV25-118. Their recorded root causes differ (compressor failure vs. donor variability), but the data point to one cause. The link between the freezer and the vector is inferred from the data, and the CAPA-26-016 root cause is contradicted by it.

**CAPAs raised from deviations (trace_link RESULTED_IN equivalents)**
- CAPA-26-008 (corrective, closed, "effective") ← DEV-26-021: FRZ-80-02 high-temperature alarm, root cause "compressor failure (age-related)". Action: replace the compressor.
- CAPA-26-016 (preventive, open) ← DEV-26-027: low %CAR+ in ENG26-01/02, root cause "suspected donor variability (low CD3%)". Action: evaluate a minimum CD3% criterion.
- CAPA-26-012 (open, past due) ← DEV-26-011: INC-03 door alarm late, root cause "door switch misaligned".
- CAPA-26-015 (closed, effectiveness "PENDING") ← DEV-26-033: PPQ26-02 low viability, root cause "operator did not confirm door latch".
- CAPA-26-019 (open) ← DEV-26-041: tubing supplier weld defect. No link to the others.

**The shared cause: FRZ-80-02 thermal excursion affecting vector lot LV25-118**
- The historian shows FRZ8002 rising from about -80 °C to about -10 °C between 20 and 23 April, and not back below -78 °C until 23 April 16:00. DEV-26-021 records a maximum of about -36 °C before relocation.
- Lot LV25-118 is stored in FRZ-80-02 (material_lot). It was used for every transduction from PD26-014 onward.
- Transductions with LV25-118 before the excursion gave FC-CAR (%CAR+) of 34.5–41.3 (PD26-014 to PD26-023).
- Transductions with LV25-118 after the excursion gave 11.9–19.8: PD26-024 (17.3), PD26-025 (14.9), PD26-026 (16.3), PD26-027 (16.0), ENG26-01 (19.8), ENG26-02 (11.9), ENG26-03 (13.9).
- Donor CD3% does not explain the drop. ENG26-01 and ENG26-02 had CD3 of 65.3% and 63.8%, similar to or better than pre-excursion batches. PD26-023 had 65.0% CD3 and %CAR+ of 35.1%. ENG26-03 shows the same drop but is not listed in DEV-26-027.
- The vector CoA functional titer (FT_TU_ML, 104 × 10⁶ TU/mL) did not change, and the MOI was nominally 5.0 in every batch. So the potency loss is not visible in the uo04 record or the titer. The mechanism is a pattern-based inference, not a confirmed finding.

**Gaps to resolve**
- CAPA-26-008 was closed as effective based only on the compressor replacement and pull-down check. Nothing in the record assesses the vector lot that was in the freezer.
- DEV-26-021 says the vector was relocated to FRZ-80-01 at 15:30 on 20 April. The historian shows FRZ-80-02 still warm through 22 April, and material_lot still lists LV25-118 in FRZ-80-02.
- No trace link connects DEV-26-021 or DEV-26-027 to LV25-118 or to the affected batches.

**Weaker, separate link:** CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015 both concern the INC-03 door (DEV-26-011 and DEV-26-033). They share equipment and failure mode, but their recorded causes are different and there is no data here to show one caused the other, so I have not counted them as the shared cause.
